references.name: text-embeddings-inference
references.procedure: POST /decode then /tokenize to check the rows survive TEI's re-tokenization; then POST /embed with the batch's 32 rows as token ids, 5 untimed then 50 timed, each timed from sending the request to reading the whole response, the p50 and p99 of TEI's x-total-time, x-tokenization-time, x-queue-time, x-inference-time headers beside it, and TEI's /metrics read before and after the timed requests for its te_batch_next_size and te_batch_next_tokens histograms; min_cosine is against the bundle's reference vectors; TEI's router built natively and run on this machine, not in a container; round trip (measured) p50 1151.012 ms, p99 1233.766 ms; TEI's own headers, whole ms, over the same requests: x-total-time p50 1145 p99 1227, x-tokenization-time p50 10 p99 19, x-queue-time p50 215 p99 357, x-inference-time p50 710 p99 1079; TEI's /metrics over the timed requests: 1600 inputs in 50 requests, 149 backend batches (te_batch_next_size's 265 samples less the 116 empty polls te_batch_next_tokens shows), 2.98 batches per request, mean batch size 10.74 inputs (batches by size, 1: 18, 2: 14, 3 to 4: 28, 5 to 8: 28, 9 to 16: 17, 17 to 32: 44); the tool ran unpinned; TEI ran unpinned with the image's thread settings: OMP_NUM_THREADS=unset, MKL_NUM_THREADS=unset, RAYON_NUM_THREADS=unset

references.name: mlx
references.procedure: MLX 0.29.3 on the machine's Python, the BERT encoder of bench/reference/mlx_reference.py with every weight cast to float32, mx.compile, mean pooling and L2 in F32, on the same token rows as a padded batch; untimed runs, then 50 timed as host wall time, each waited for with mx.eval, the rows already on the device and the vectors not read back: min 150.2219 ms, mean 152.8960 ms. min_cosine is against each row's expected vector. Host load averages before the runs 2.20 3.02 4.60.
